text: Abstract. We study the memory-bandwidth bottleneck of autoregressive decoding at million-token context lengths. We show that for grouped-query architectures the cache-read volume per emitted token dominates end-to-end latency once the context exceeds a hardware-dependent threshold, and we derive a closed-form expression for that threshold in terms of HBM bandwidth, group ratio, and head dimension. Experiments on rack-scale accelerators validate the model within 7 percent.

Mitochondria are membrane-bound organelles that generate most of the chemical energy needed to power a eukaryotic cell's biochemical reactions, stored in the form of adenosine triphosphate. They retain their own circular genome, inherited maternally in most species, a property that has made mitochondrial DNA a standard marker for tracing lineage and population movements over evolutionary timescales.

Abstract. Solid-state electrolytes promise safer high-density batteries, but interfacial resistance between the electrolyte and lithium-metal anodes remains the limiting factor. We report a sintering protocol that produces a conformal garnet interface, reducing interfacial resistance by an order of magnitude at room temperature and sustaining one thousand plating cycles without dendrite penetration in symmetric-cell tests.
